historical_reviews.deepseek: The reads are non-destructive, but the path is assumed and full FRU output can disclose multiple serial and asset identifiers.

historical_reviews.v3_1: Treats a serial match as a three-way identity proof among the selected product FRU, validated UI object and controlled inventory record.

original_test_intent: Verify that the Product Serial in the selected product FRU is readable, correct and identical to the product serial shown by the authoritative BMC UI/OEM inventory.
original_method: Bind one physical product and FRU record, securely collect the FRU and matching UI/API field, protect raw identifiers, and compare both with the authoritative asset inventory.
manual_activity: Supply the authoritative inventory serial, product-resource mapping and approved serial normalization/redaction policy; no physical action is required.
required_inputs: Approved serial normalization and masking policy
Read-only credential handle and trusted CA
safety_requirements: Use read-only FRU and API operations
Never write FRU or issue PATCH/raw mutations
Never place passwords in argv or evidence
Mask unrelated serials and asset fields
Do not equate board/chassis serials with Product Serial
Stop on duplicate, blank or replacement-serial ambiguity
agent_execution_scope: Resolve the matching UI/API product object
Capture status-bearing responses into protected storage
Extract only the scoped Product Serial
Compare FRU, UI and inventory values

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `ipmitool fru print` can expose Product Serial, but a full unredacted dump broadens disclosure and `.Product.SerialNumber` at the proposed chassis URI is not validated. Missing-path text is an error, not evidence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use secure read-only queries for the bound product FRU and validated UI/API serial property; store raw identifiers under access control and compare masked results with the authoritative asset record.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The FRU-list inspection, Product Serial field, UI agreement criterion and 2/0-minute timing are preserved; identity, mapping and privacy rules are made explicit.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a product-scoped serial comparator with resource provenance, protected raw values, masked reports and immutable inventory-reference version.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds physical-asset binding and evidence minimization rather than returning a full FRU dump for visual confirmation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects wrong-product, duplicate and replacement serial conditions while retaining the intended read-only comparison.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Serials are sensitive asset identifiers; over-normalization or cross-object comparison can silently accept the wrong unit.

project_override_considerations: Product Serial is distinct from board, chassis, GPU and other component serials. The selected UI object must represent the same physical product as the FRU record.
expected_evidence: Selected product FRU and UI/API object
No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master consistently requests Product Serial FRU/UI agreement. The absent asset oracle, mapping and privacy policy are execution prerequisites, not contradictory requirements.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The target field and read-only comparison are clear; identity, inventory and secure evidence packages are obtainable through the normal request path.

review_improvement: Prevents disclosure of unrelated asset data and false agreement between a product serial and a component or wrong-chassis serial.
independent_technical_reasoning: A serial number is only meaningful when bound to one physical product and source object. Because a full FRU listing contains several component identities, field-name equality alone cannot establish provenance. The automation must bind the product, protect raw identifiers and compare against controlled inventory; these finite inputs justify REQUIRES rather than BLOCKED.
